record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: For a Schrödinger operator H = H0 + V(x) = -∆ + V(x) with localized time-independent potential and complete bounded wave operators Ω±, how can compactness of localized outgoing wave-operator expressions be related to transmission eigenvalues? Can one prove discreteness of the transmission-eigenvalue set, use approximate knowledge of Ω to construct candidate transparent frequencies k, and extend the method to time-dependent or nonlinear interactions?

evidence.quote: The question is how to use these observations to relate it to the notion of transmission eigenvalues ? Can one use the above compactness to prove the discreteness of the set of transmission eigenvalues? Knowing Ω, even approximately, how to get an approximate candidate for transparent k? We know how to construct Ω for time dependent and nonlinear interactions. How to use this knowledge for the construction of transparency?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H_0 = -\Delta$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and let $V \in L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ be a real-valued, compactly supported (or sufficiently rapidly decaying) time-independent potential, and set $H = H_0 + V$. Assume that the wave operators
$$\Omega_\pm := \mathrm{s\text{-}lim}_{t\to\mp\infty} e^{itH} e^{-itH_0}$$
exist, are bounded on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, and are complete (so that $\Omega_\pm$ are unitary from $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ onto the absolutely continuous subspace of $H$). For a bounded open set $\mathcal{O} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ containing $\mathrm{supp}\,V$, let $\chi_\mathcal{O}$ denote multiplication by the indicator of $\mathcal{O}$, and consider localized expressions of the form $\chi_\mathcal{O}(\Omega_\pm - I)\chi_\mathcal{O}$ or related localizations of the scattering identity.

A real number $k^2 > 0$ is called a (real) transmission eigenvalue (in the sense relevant to transparency) if there exists a nontrivial pair $(u, v)$ of solutions to $(-\Delta + V)u = k^2 u$ and $-\Delta v = k^2 v$ in $\mathcal{O}$ such that $u = v$ and $\partial_\nu u = \partial_\nu v$ on $\partial \mathcal{O}$. Equivalently, $k$ corresponds to a "transparent frequency" if there is a free wave that, after interaction with $V$, produces no scattered field outside $\mathcal{O}$.

Address the following:

(a) Show that the compactness of the localized wave-operator difference $\chi_\mathcal{O}(\Omega_\pm - I)\chi_\mathcal{O}$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ implies the discreteness of the set of real transmission eigenvalues associated with $(H_0, H, \mathcal{O})$, with no finite accumulation point in $(0,\infty)$.

(b) Given only approximate knowledge of $\Omega_\pm$ (in operator norm, up to a small error), construct an explicit procedure that produces candidate transparent frequencies $k$ together with quantitative error bounds.

(c) Extend the construction in (a)–(b) to settings where the interaction is time-dependent (so $V = V(t,x)$ with appropriate decay) and to nonlinear interactions for which bounded, complete wave operators $\Omega_\pm$ have been established, formulating an appropriate notion of transparency in those settings.
artifact.status_search_result: The proposed program—linking compactness of localized wave-operator expressions to discreteness of transmission eigenvalues, constructing transparent frequencies from approximate wave operators, and extending to time-dependent/nonlinear interactions—is posed as a set of open questions. Discreteness of transmission eigenvalues is known under various hypotheses (e.g., via upper-triangular compact operators and via a T-coercivity/sign-changing-contrast approach), and transparent potentials are known to exist in special classes, but the unified wave-operator-based framework requested, especially the nonlinear/time-dependent extension, has not been carried out in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: Discreteness of Transmission Eigenvalues via Upper Triangular Compact Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes discreteness of transmission eigenvalues using compact-operator techniques, but not via localized wave operators.
status_evidence.claim: Discreteness results exist under specific hypotheses, supporting that part (a) is plausible but not in the wave-operator form requested.

status_evidence.title: Transparent Scatterers and Transmission Eigenvalues
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses transparent potentials and links to transmission eigenvalues; gives examples (Schwartz-class transparent potentials in 2D, multipoint potentials).
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between transparency and transmission eigenvalues is an active research topic with the general program still open.

status_evidence.title: Discreteness of interior transmission eigenvalues revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Revisits discreteness results for interior transmission eigenvalues under contrast assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Various conditional discreteness results exist, but a wave-operator-compactness-based proof addressing time-dependent and nonlinear cases is not established.
